intro.text: 今天这批内容有一条清晰的张力线：工具层在拼命补课——Codex 负责人公开征集「我们明显该做却没做的事」，Google 一口气列了 Gemini 十项改进进度；而创业圈在集体重算护城河——Nikunj 说整个 AI 栈从上到下没人有 moat，Levie 说数据才是未来资产负债表上的资产，No Priors 里 Sarah Guo 和 Elad Gil 则在认真算「未来五年还能长出几个万亿美元公司」。工具越强，越逼着每个人回答同一个问题：你到底在为什么创造价值。

archive.title: 护城河之辩日报
archive.desc: 模型与工具层集体补课的同时，创业圈在重新定义护城河：全栈无 moat 论、数据资产化、万亿美元公司还剩几个，以及创始人野心是否正在悄悄缩水。

sections.title: Platforms Catching Up / 平台补课进行时
sections.desc: Codex 和 Gemini 都公开了下一步的改进清单——工具层正在以前所未有的速度回应真实反馈。

rewrite: Thibault Sottiaux, who leads Codex & ChatGPT at OpenAI, posted the kind of question that pulls 4,700+ replies: what is an obvious thing we should do with Codex, the API or our models that we just haven't done yet? Something 100% within reach that we seem to be missing?

It's a masterclass in open-ended product fishing: instead of announcing features, he asked the community to write his roadmap. 3.7k likes and thousands of replies later, the thread is a goldmine of unmet needs, and the message is clear: the fastest way to find the next obvious feature is to ask the people who use it daily.
original: What is an obvious thing that we should do with Codex, API or our models that we should just do but haven't yet? What is 100% within reach, but we just seem to be missing?

rewrite: OpenAI Codex 与 ChatGPT 负责人 Thibault Sottiaux 抛出了一个收获 4700+ 回复的问题：Codex、API 或我们的模型，有什么「显而易见、完全够得着、但就是一直没做」的事？
这是一次教科书级的开放式产品调研：不宣布功能，而是让社区帮他写路线图。3726 个赞和几千条回复之后，这条 thread 成了一座未被满足需求的富矿。信息也很明确：想找到下一个显而易见的 feature，最快的方式是去问每天在用的人。
original: Codex、API 或我们的模型，有什么明显该做但我们一直没做的事？什么完全在我们的能力范围内，却好像一直被我们漏掉了？

rewrite: Josh Woodward, VP at Google leading Gemini, circled back on an earlier 'what should we improve' thread with a 10-point status update: revamped Workspace tools testing in 1-2 weeks, 3.7 Flash showing better tool calling, a new 'Projects' design done and being implemented, 49 connectors supported and counting, and a batch of items marked done, including fixes to the biggest over-triggering bugs.

The pattern worth noticing: most items are about tool use and connectors, not raw model quality. Google is clearly racing to turn Gemini into a better agent platform, and it's shipping at a visible cadence, item by item, in public.
original: Circling back on this with some updates... What's the next set of things we can improve to make your Gemini experience even better? #1: Testing revamped Workspace tools in 1-2 weeks #2: 3.7 Flash showed improvements in tool calling, more coming here #3: New "Projects" design done, implementing now #4: 49 connectors (and counting) supported now #5: Backend work done, frontend work started #6: Done #7: Done #8: Done #9: Done #10: Done, fixed the biggest over-triggering bugs

rewrite: Google VP（负责 Gemini）的 Josh Woodward 跟进之前那条「Gemini 还该改进什么」的征集帖，给出十项进度更新：重构版 Workspace 工具 1-2 周内开测，3.7 Flash 在工具调用上有进步，新版 Projects 设计已完成、正在开发，连接器已支持 49 个（还在增加），多项直接标了「已完成」，包括修掉最大的过度触发 bug。
值得注意的共性：大部分条目都围绕工具调用和连接器，而不是模型原始能力。Google 明显在把 Gemini 往 agent 平台方向猛推，而且保持着一项一项、在公开场合看得见的发布节奏。

sections.title: Tools & New Moves / 工具与新玩法
sections.desc: 从 agent 原生的代码托管，到一条 /design 命令做设计，再到开源的个人 AGI——把创意和流程变成可编辑的代码正在成为默认姿势。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch announced the loop is now complete: you can host your repos in Cursor Origin and deploy to Vercel straight from there, with Cursor Origin itself running on Vercel. 'And unlike GitHub, it's online,' he jokes.

3.6k likes say it all: the coding-agent world is eating the source-of-truth layer. When your IDE, your repo host and your deploy target all live inside one agent-native stack, GitHub's position as the neutral middleman starts to look very different.
original: You can now host your repos in Cursor Origin and deploy to Vercel via Cursor Origin which is itself hosted on Vercel. And unlike GitHub, it's online 😁

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 宣布闭环打通：你可以在 Cursor Origin 里托管仓库，并直接从 Origin 部署到 Vercel——而 Cursor Origin 本身就跑在 Vercel 上。「而且不像 GitHub，它是在线的。」他开玩笑说。
3600 个赞说明一切：coding agent 的世界正在吃掉「代码真相源」这一层。当 IDE、代码托管和部署目标全都长在同一个 agent 原生栈里，GitHub 作为中立中间人的位置就开始变得可疑了。
original: 你现在可以在 Cursor Origin 里托管仓库，并经由 Cursor Origin（它本身托管在 Vercel 上）部署到 Vercel。而且不像 GitHub，它是在线的 😁

rewrite: Thariq, who works on Claude Code at Anthropic, posted the shortest possible demo: go into Claude Code and type /design <something you want to design>. That's it. 880 likes for a two-line post, which tells you how real the appetite for design-via-code is.

It fits the argument he's been making: code is easier to edit, easier to nudge in the direction you want, and easier to export into existing tools. When design tokens, layouts and even 3D scenes are expressed as code, every output stays malleable, which is something static pixels never are.
original: go into CC and type /design <something you want to design> do it rn

rewrite: 在 Anthropic 做 Claude Code 的 Thariq 发了一条最短的演示帖：打开 Claude Code，输入 /design <你想设计的东西>，就完了。一条两行字的帖子拿到 880 赞——大家对「用代码做设计」的渴望是真的。
这和他一直在讲的逻辑一致：代码的好处是容易编辑、能朝你想要的任何方向微调、还能导出到现有工具。当设计 token、版式和 3D 场景都以代码表达时，所有产出都保持可塑——这是静态像素永远做不到的。
original: 进 CC（Claude Code）输入 /design <你想设计的东西>，现在就去试。

rewrite: Y Combinator President & CEO Garry Tan open-sourced his Personal AGI setup: a GitHub repo with 70 of his proven skills plus the beginnings of a Karpathy-style knowledge wiki, MIT-licensed and free. It works with your existing Claude Code or Codex subscription, just make a new directory and paste an image into CC/Codex to set up your agent repo.

Low engagement, high signal for builders: this is a concrete, copyable starting point for turning your own accumulated writing and workflows into an agent's memory, straight from one of the most visible operator-CEOs in the Valley.
original: This is my open source to help you create your own Personal AGI as mentioned at my Startup School talk earlier this year

What do you get? A private github repo with 70 of my proven skills and the beginnings of your Karpathy-style knowledge wiki. Read the full docs in the README. All of this is MIT-licensed open source and free.

rewrite: YC 总裁兼 CEO Garry Tan 把他自己的「Personal AGI」开源了：一个 GitHub 仓库，包含 70 个他验证过的 skills，外加一个 Karpathy 式知识 wiki 的雏形，MIT 协议、完全免费。直接复用你现有的 Claude Code 或 Codex 订阅——新建一个目录，把一张图贴进 CC/Codex，它就会帮你搭好 agent 仓库。
点赞不多，但对 builder 来说信号很强：这是一份可以直接抄的起点，把你多年积累的文字和工作流变成 agent 的记忆——来自湾区最能打的 operator-CEO 之一。

sections.title: The Moat Debate / 护城河之辩
sections.desc: 全栈无护城河论、数据进资产负债表、万亿美元公司的真实数量——创业圈在重新定义什么才值得建。

rewrite: The takeaway: don't expect many new trillion-dollar companies over the next five years, and if your ambition has quietly shrunk to 'safe niches,' that may be the bigger risk than the labs.

Sarah Guo and Elad Gil do the market-cap math: three companies went from roughly zero to a trillion in five years (Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceX), but that was punctuated equilibrium, a burst rather than a trend. A trillion-dollar company needs $50-100B of real revenue; a $10B company is a different order of magnitude entirely. Their sharper worry: too many excellent founders are fleeing to niche markets out of fear of the labs. 'I am more often disappointed right now that founders are being less ambitious than they could be.'

They get practical too: hold a pre-scheduled, unemotional 'should we exit' board conversation every six months, because one year of AI time is like three to four normal years, and the underlying fact set is changing faster than it ever has. As for the 'code solved in six months, light RSI by next year' belief circulating in the labs: take it seriously, but remember that recursive self-improvement has been 'eighteen months away' for five straight years.
original: There's still a lot of $100,000,000,000 companies to be built, but multi trillion dollar companies are kind of hard to get to.
I am more often disappointed right now that founders are being less ambitious than they could be.
Every year of AI time is like three to four years of normal cycle time... you should double check your thinking more frequently because the underlying fact set is changing faster than it ever has.

rewrite: 一句话结论：未来五年别指望长出很多新的万亿美元公司——而如果你的野心已经在「安全的小众市场」里悄悄缩水，那可能比实验室的威胁更大。

Sarah Guo 和 Elad Gil 算了笔市值账：五年内三家公司从接近零冲到万亿美元（Anthropic、OpenAI、SpaceX），但那是「间断平衡」——一次爆发，不是常态。万亿美元公司需要 500-1000 亿美元的真实营收；百亿美元公司和它是完全不同的数量级。他们更尖锐的担忧是：太多优秀创始人因为害怕实验室而逃进小众市场。「现在我更常感到失望的是，创始人比他们本可以做到的更不进取。」
他们也很务实：每六个月开一次预先排期、不带情绪的「该不该卖公司」董事会讨论——因为 AI 的一年相当于正常周期的三四年，底层事实的变化速度前所未有，判断也该更频繁地复查。至于实验室圈子里流传的「6 个月解决代码、明年出现轻量 RSI」：认真对待，但记住「递归自我改进」已经连续五年被喊「还有 18 个月」了。
original: 能建成的百亿美元公司还有很多，但万亿美元级别的公司真的很难够到。
现在我更常感到失望的是，创始人比他们本可以做到的更不进取。
AI 的一年相当于正常周期的三四年……你应该更频繁地复查自己的判断，因为底层事实的变化速度前所未有。

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari, partner at FPV Ventures, dropped a listicle-style hot take that hit like a bomb: the models have no moat, the IDEs have no moat, the harnesses, app builders, wrappers, inference providers, voice layers, data labeling companies, AI infrastructure, neoclouds, generative media, 'apparently nobody in AI has a moat, except the venture firm.'

1.5k likes and a furious comment section later, the point lands: when every layer is one API call away from commoditization, durable value migrates to whoever owns distribution, brand or the underlying asset. It rhymes with Aaron Levie's 'data as a balance sheet asset' take in this same issue.
original: the models have no moat (OpenAI, Anthropic, XAI) the IDEs have no moat (Cursor, Windsurf) the harnesses have no moat (Cognition, Factory, LangChain) the app builders have no moat (Replit, Lovable, Bolt) the wrappers have no moat (Harvey, Abridge, OpenEvidence) the inference providers have no moat (Together, Fireworks, Groq) the voice layer has no moat (Sierra, Decagon, ElevenLabs) the data labeling companies have no moat (Scale, Surge, Mercor) the AI infrastructure has no moat (Baseten, Modal, Railway) the neoclouds have no moat (CoreWeave, Lambda, Crusoe) the generative media companies have no moat (Runway, Higgsfield, Suno) apparently nobody in AI has a moat except the venture firm ☠️

rewrite: FPV Ventures 合伙人 Nikunj Kothari 这条清单体暴论炸开了锅：模型没有护城河，IDE 没有护城河，harness、应用搭建器、套壳应用、推理供应商、语音层、数据标注公司、AI 基础设施、neocloud、生成式媒体——「显然 AI 圈谁都没有护城河，除了风投公司。」
1483 个赞加评论区混战之后，核心论点其实很扎实：当每一层都离「一个 API 调用」只有一步之遥，持久价值正在流向掌握分发、品牌或底层资产的人——这个主题和本期 Levie 的「数据进资产负债表」论正好互相印证。
original: 模型没有护城河（OpenAI、Anthropic、XAI）；IDE 没有（Cursor、Windsurf）；harness 没有（Cognition、Factory、LangChain）；应用搭建没有（Replit、Lovable、Bolt）；套壳没有（Harvey、Abridge、OpenEvidence）；推理供应商没有（Together、Fireworks、Groq）；语音层没有（Sierra、Decagon、ElevenLabs）；数据标注没有（Scale、Surge、Mercor）；AI 基础设施没有（Baseten、Modal、Railway）；neocloud 没有（CoreWeave、Lambda、Crusoe）；生成式媒体没有（Runway、Higgsfield、Suno）。显然 AI 圈谁都没有护城河——除了风投公司 ☠️

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie, reacting to a data sale, delivers the sharpest business line of the day: 'when you hear that data is the new oil, this is ultimately what that looks like. AI has such a thirst for data that we're entering an era where it's valuable almost in any form. In a world of AI, information actually belongs as an asset on the balance sheet.'

His conclusion is the strategic one: how companies manage and mine their organizational intelligence will be one of the deciding factors for competitiveness and value creation. If the agents can't get good without your data, then your data just became your most underpriced asset.
original: When you hear that data is the new oil, this is ultimately what that looks like. AI has such a thirst for data that we're entering an era where it's valuable almost in any form. In a world of AI, information actually belongs as an asset on the balance sheet. This data sale is just one example of the implications of what that will look like. Ultimately, the way that companies manage and mine their organization's intelligence will be one of the deciding factors for competitiveness and value creation in the future.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 看到一笔数据交易后，给出了今天最锋利的一句商业判断：「当人们说数据是新石油，最终就是这样的图景。AI 对数据的渴求，让我们进入了一个数据几乎以任何形态都有价值的时代。在 AI 的世界里，信息真的应该作为资产出现在资产负债表上。」
他的结论才是关键：公司如何管理和开采自己的组织智能，将成为未来竞争力和价值创造的决定性因素之一。如果 agent 离开你的数据就变不好用，你的数据就变成了被严重低估的资产。
original: 当你听到「数据是新石油」，最终就是这种图景。AI 对数据的渴求，让我们进入数据几乎以任何形态都有价值的时代。在 AI 的世界里，信息真的应该作为资产进入资产负债表。这笔数据交易只是这种图景的一个例子。最终，公司如何管理和开采组织智能，将成为未来竞争力和价值创造的决定性因素之一。

sections.title: Engineering & Craft / 工程与手艺
sections.desc: eval 怎么练、创意工作该交给哪种模型——两条来自一线的实操判断。

rewrite: Madhu Guru, Senior Director of AI at Meta (previously led Gemini, Veo and Nano Banana at Google), offers a refreshingly concrete method for getting good at evals: take a workflow you know really well and figure out how to make its quality measurable. Study the actual traces, the sequence of prompts typical users have and what good responses look like at each step and end-to-end.

Then capture the traces where your product fails: messy tool-call responses, missing context. Once you have a good eval, make it easy to run repeatedly and automatically, and keep it mirroring live traffic as user patterns evolve. That's the difference between 'we have evals' and 'our evals track reality.'
original: The best way to get good at evals is to take a workflow you know really well and figure out how to make its quality measurable. Study the actual traces - the sequence of prompts typical users have, what good responses would look like at each step and for the end to end outcome. Study where your product fails and create traces that capture them - messy tool call responses, missing context etc. Once you have a good eval, think about how you would make it easy to run repeatedly and automatically. Once you have that, think about how you will ensure your eval continues to mirror live traffic as your users patterns evolve.

rewrite: Meta AI 高级总监 Madhu Guru（之前在 Google 带过 Gemini、Veo 和 Nano Banana）给出了一个异常务实的「怎么做好 eval」方法论：选一个你非常熟悉的工作流，想办法让它的质量变得可测量。去研究真实 traces——典型用户会有一连串什么样的 prompt，每一步和端到端的好的回答应该长什么样。
然后再把你产品失败的 traces 也抓进来：混乱的工具调用响应、缺失的上下文。有了好 eval 之后，想清楚怎么让它能反复自动运行，并且持续镜像真实流量，因为用户模式会变。这就是「我们有 eval」和「我们的 eval 跟得上现实」之间的区别。
original: 练好 eval 的最好方法：选一个你非常熟悉的工作流，想办法让它的质量可测量。研究真实 traces——典型用户的一系列 prompt、每一步和端到端的好回答应该是什么样。研究你产品失败的地方，创建能捕捉它们的 traces——混乱的工具调用响应、缺失上下文等。有了好的 eval，再想怎么让它易于反复自动运行。然后想怎么让 eval 持续镜像真实流量，因为用户模式会演化。

rewrite: Thariq notes that the recent wave of procedural-generation art, video editing and 3D game demos has updated his prior: LLM coding models are better at a lot of creative work than diffusion models.

It's a quiet but telling inversion. The same models that 'write code' can now express visual ideas through code, which is editable, composable and exportable, and creative tools built on next-token prediction are starting to beat pixel generators on controllability. 470 likes suggest he's not alone in noticing.
original: all of the recent proc gen art, video editing and 3d game demos recently have made me update towards LLM coding models being better at a lot of creative work than diffusion models

rewrite: Thariq 说最近一波程序化生成艺术、视频剪辑和 3D 游戏 demo 让他更新了判断：LLM 编码模型在很多创意工作上已经比扩散模型做得更好。
这是一个安静但意味深长的反转：那些「写代码」的模型现在能通过代码表达视觉想法，而代码是可编辑、可组合、可导出的。基于 next-token 预测的创意工具开始在可控性上击败像素生成器——470 个赞说明注意到这一点的不只他一个。
original: 最近所有的程序化生成艺术、视频剪辑和 3D 游戏 demo，让我更新了判断：LLM 编码模型在很多创意工作上会比扩散模型做得更好。
